about.intro: Every photo you take carries a hidden diary — where you were, which camera you used, the exact second you pressed the shutter. Most people never know it's there. PureClear exists so anyone can wipe that diary clean in seconds — without uploading a thing, and without trusting anyone.
about.problemTitle: Metadata is invisible. Its consequences aren't.
about.problemBody: A single shared photo can reveal your home address through GPS coordinates, your daily routine through timestamps, and your expensive gear through camera serials. Journalists, activists, sellers, parents — anyone sharing photos online is exposed. And the tools to fix it were either complicated, degraded your photos, or quietly uploaded your files to someone else's server.
about.p1b: GPS coordinates embedded in photos can pinpoint your home, your kid's school, or a confidential meeting spot — to anyone who downloads the image.
about.p2b: Camera model, serial numbers and software versions quietly identify your gear — and sometimes, you.
about.p3b: Timestamps and edit history reconstruct your routine. You share a moment; you leak a pattern.
about.principlesTitle: Built the way privacy should be.
about.pr1b: Every byte is processed in your browser with WebAssembly. There is no server to trust, because no server is ever involved.
about.pr2b: No tiers, no watermarks, no 'pro' unlock. Cleaning your own files shouldn't cost anything.
about.pr3b: No sign-ups, no cookies following you around, no analytics. We can't sell data we never see.
about.pr4b: Only the metadata is removed. Your pixels, quality and resolution stay exactly as they were.
about.ctaBody: Drop a photo in. See what's hiding inside. Wipe it in one click.
privacy.intro: PureClear is designed so there is nothing to collect, nothing to store, and nothing to breach. Here's exactly what happens — and what doesn't — when you use it.
privacy.imageAlt: Smartphone protected by a glowing privacy shield with a lock
privacy.s1t: Your files never leave your browser
privacy.s1b: When you drop a file into PureClear, it is read and processed entirely on your device, using WebAssembly running locally in your browser tab. No file, thumbnail or metadata is transmitted to any server — ours or anyone else's. You can verify this yourself: disconnect from the internet after the page loads, and everything still works.
privacy.s2b: There is nothing to sign up for and no login. Without accounts there is no profile to build, no email to leak, and no password to steal.
privacy.s3b: We don't run analytics, advertising trackers or fingerprinting scripts, and we don't use cookies to follow you across the web. Your visit is your business.
privacy.s4b: We keep no logs of the files you process — no metadata, no records tied to your IP. When you close the tab, everything is gone. The way it should be.
privacy.s5b: Honesty matters: once you share a cleaned file, we can't control what others do with it. And stripping metadata removes the hidden data, not anonymity itself — faces, landmarks and context can still identify. PureClear removes the invisible; stay thoughtful about the visible.
privacy.ctaBody: Drop a file and see what was hiding inside it.
